skills.name: 观照万象
skills.direction: 连体神目纹：大眼、对扣角勾、赭金墨瞳。
skills.generationPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE original emblematic totem skill icon for a Chinese fantasy game, intended for 24–40px.
Primary request: a recognizable symbolic motif, with the iconic solidity and integrated animal-organ construction of ancient emblems, painted using highly reduced Chinese xieyi ink. The image must have a named, instantly recognizable SUBJECT, not arbitrary calligraphic strokes. Design the entire silhouette as a tight interconnected motif, with a clear hierarchy, repeated short hooked forms, and large meaningful transparent cutouts. Combine rounded structural masses with angular terminals. Keep it extremely legible as a small game icon.
Medium: warm charcoal Chinese ink; confident thick brush planes, small directional patches of natural dry brush and warm gray wash. The frozen project ink portrait references inform only the broad brush scale, charcoal warmth and variation, not human figures. Most of the shape is strong readable ink, with one clear area of restrained mineral color. No uniform thin outline and no brush texture covering every surface. Flat symbolic construction; not a metallic object and not a realistic creature illustration.
Composition: square canvas, ONE centered complete glyph; width or height occupies about 80% of canvas with safe margins. Compact mass and substantial stroke thickness; no long thin tails. True transparent background and true transparent internal negative space.
Constraints: original fantasy symbol. Draw only the described subject. No generic outer badge circle or square, frame, paper rectangle, text, pseudowriting, digits, seal, watermark, backdrop or checkerboard. No complex ornamental fill, micro patterns, dense splatter, glow, gradient, 3D material or fine hairlike ends. Short attached ornaments are part of the subject, never separate floating triangles. No extra motifs or tiny scenes.
Subject: 观照万象 — an ancient divine-eye totem symbolizing an overarching gaze that gathers several offensive powers. ONE very large horizontal almond eye set within a compact symmetrical, slightly squared-diamond eye-mask motif. A pair of stout mirrored hooked brow/cheek forms directly constitute the upper and lower outline of the eye. At the left and right corners they turn into SHORT inward curling corner-hooks; above them two VERY SHORT attached angular horn tabs echo the construction. All these forms are CONNECTED into one cohesive oracle-eye silhouette, not an eye surrounded by disconnected triangles. The eye opening is an ample clean almond-shaped transparent cutout. At its center is one simple flat ochre-gold iris disc with a small solid charcoal pupil; no realistic highlights. The eye fills about 60% of the total width. Paired corner hooks feel like greatly simplified Chinese bronze animal-mask geometry translated into brush ink, broad and open rather than intricate. Only one eye, no human face, no teeth. Its overall silhouette is a broad compact rhombus with squared hooked corners, not a sunburst, logo eye or decorative mandala. Eye/pupil is the decisive focal point. About six to eight stout primary forms, very little surface texture.

skills.direction: 藏云法芒纹：对扣云勾藏势，一枚紫墨法芒骤出。

The positive and negative shapes fit tightly together like an old emblem: concealed cloud curls hold and open into a sudden spell flash. Compact nearly round asymmetric silhouette, broad chunky points, no long projecting blade. At 24px the cloud and four-point flash must be clearly different shapes. This is a fantasy design metaphor for concealed power, not lightning-element magic: no zigzag bolt or weather scene. No portal, sword, spear, literal arrow, eye, orb, realistic smoke, many small stars, petals, runes or extra flourishes. About five bold primary forms maximum.
skills.refinementPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the single provided transparent 出奇制胜 skill icon.
Primary request: keep its coherent Chinese cloud-and-spell totem concept but SIMPLIFY AND IMPROVE 24px readability.
Change ONLY the cloud construction and spell flare strength. Replace the many overlapping cloud petals/curls with EXACTLY TWO broad opposing Chinese auspicious-cloud hooked lobes, interlocking into a compact broken-ring silhouette with two VERY LARGE clean transparent C-shaped internal cutouts. Remove all extra tiny curling ends and subsidiary cloud petals. The two cloud units should be obvious as a repeated connected motif, strong warm-charcoal ink with a little gray wash and restrained local dry-brush variation.
Make the ONE four-pointed diamond-shaped spell flash about 40–45% of total glyph width, in substantial muted DARK gray-violet mineral ink so it remains identifiable at 24px. The whole four-point flash should be flat violet ink, with only subtle small tonal variation: REMOVE the white center, REMOVE bevel-like cream highlights and any white star-within-star. Keep its four points short and thick, not long thin lines; one upper-right point can be slightly emphasized. It emerges from the cloud gap and meets a cloud at one root, forming a complete simple symbol rather than a separate sticker. Cloud should surround the lower-left part of the flare, giving a dynamic reveal.
Preserve: ONE original connected compact motif, Chinese xieyi broad ink brush medium, black/gray and muted violet palette, square canvas, centered full glyph, true transparent exterior and all unpainted interior spaces. Outer width/height roughly80% with safe margins. Do not repaint as a vector, wood carving, metal object or realistic cloud; no all-over scratch texture.
Avoid: decorative extra swirls, lots of lobes, white pigment streaks simulating relief lighting, glow, gradients, paper, checkerboard, border, circular badge base, text, seal, tiny stars, lightning bolt, weapon, literal doorway or arrow. This is a simplified cloud motif exposing one strong spell flare.
